explanation: Unlike Buddhist cultures such as Thailand, where the head is considered spiritually sacred, Russian culture has no documented religious or folk taboo against touching the head. That said, patting an adult on the head is still generally seen as overly familiar or condescending outside of close relationships, much as it would be in most Western countries.
local_tip: Avoid patting an adult's head unless you're close friends or family; a handshake or a pat on the shoulder is a safer default.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body, and touching it is a major taboo.
Touching an adult's head is generally avoided due to spiritual beliefs about the head, though patting a child's head is common.
Patting someone on the head can read as condescending outside of close friendships or family.
